headerDisplay:
Exposes your Alarm.com security panel and sensors in HomeKit.

If two-factor authentication is enabled — and it should be — supply the `twoFactorAuthenticationId` browser cookie (not a six-digit authenticator code). Capture steps: [docs/AUTH.md](https://github.com/tbaur/homebridge-myalarmcom/blob/main/docs/AUTH.md).
footerDisplay: Alarm.com may lock accounts that poll or sign in too aggressively, and a locked account also loses the Alarm.com app. The intervals below are enforced at safe minimums for that reason.

name.title: Name
name.description: Name Homebridge shows for this platform in its log.

username.title: Username
username.description: The username you sign in to Alarm.com with. Usually an email address, but any Alarm.com login works.

password.title: Password
password.description: Your Alarm.com password. Consider creating a separate, limited Alarm.com login for this plugin rather than using your primary account.

twoFactorAuthenticationId.title: Two-Factor Cookie
twoFactorAuthenticationId.description: The value of the `twoFactorAuthenticationId` browser cookie from a signed-in Alarm.com session. Treat this as a password: it bypasses two-factor authentication on its own. A six-digit authenticator code is rejected, as is a whole cookie header — paste only this one cookie’s value. Leave blank only if the account has two-factor disabled.

pollIntervalSeconds.title: Poll Interval (seconds)
pollIntervalSeconds.description: How often to re-read all device state. Allowed range 60–86400 (24h). Values outside that range are clamped.

authIntervalMinutes.title: Re-authentication Interval (minutes)
authIntervalMinutes.description: How long a session is reused before signing in again. Allowed range 10–1440 (24h). Values outside that range are clamped.

useEventStream.title: Use push events
useEventStream.description: Subscribe to Alarm.com's event stream so sensor changes reach HomeKit within a second or two instead of waiting for the next poll. Polling continues as a fallback.

includeUnmonitoredSensors.title: Include unmonitored sensors
includeUnmonitoredSensors.description: Expose sensors that Alarm.com reports as having monitoring disabled. These are hidden by default because their readings may not be maintained. Exposed sensors are marked inactive in HomeKit rather than appearing normal, because an unsupervised sensor’s state cannot be trusted.

ignoredDeviceIds.title: Ignored Device IDs
ignoredDeviceIds.description: Alarm.com device IDs to leave out of HomeKit entirely. Each ID is shown in the log when its accessory is added, and is also the accessory’s Serial Number in the Home app.

debug.title: Debug logging
debug.description: Emit verbose diagnostics. Also requires Homebridge Debug Mode (the -D flag, or Settings → Homebridge Debug Mode): Homebridge discards DEBUG lines otherwise, so this option alone produces no extra output. Credentials and cookies are redacted, but device names and Alarm.com identifiers are not, so a debug log describes your home’s layout and activity. Review any log before sharing it.

diagnosticsInterval.title: Diagnostics interval (seconds)
diagnosticsInterval.description: Seconds between health/activity heartbeats in the Homebridge log. `0` disables (default). Allowed range 0–86400 (24h); values 1–29 are raised to 30. At 30 that is roughly 2,880 lines a day, so prefer 300 or more unless you are actively debugging. Boot and shutdown snapshots are included when enabled. Credentials are never included.
